articles.headline: Sanofi's $41B Insmed buy biggest since Pfizer/Seagen
articles.summary: Sanofi's new CEO Paul Hudson struck the largest pharma deal of 2026 with a $41B acquisition of Insmed, surpassing the Pfizer/Seagen deal in scale, with Insmed's rare-disease portfolio set to bolster Sanofi's immunology and inflammation franchise alongside its Dupixent blockbuster. In a separate catalyst, BridgeBio received FDA approval for Welgemda (its limb-girdle muscular dystrophy therapy), marking the first targeted treatment for the rare muscle disease. The newsletter also notes Roche/Genentech's second consecutive breast cancer approval in a week for its oral SERD Wilserdly.
articles.why_it_matters: The Sanofi/Insmed deal sets a fresh valuation benchmark for rare-disease and immunology assets and signals that large-cap acquirers are back in the market at scale, while BridgeBio's first FDA approval (BBIO) is a direct near-term catalyst for the coverage universe.

articles.headline: Modeling Meta, Part 3: The Compute Bill, and Valuation
articles.summary: The third installment of MBI Deep Dives' Meta series builds a detailed cost model anchored in gigawatts of compute, projecting Meta's fleet from 7 GW today to ~37 GW by 2035, with training for Meta Superintelligence Labs consuming nearly half. The piece analyzes non-cancelable capex commitments (~$121B due in 2027), potential excess capacity monetization (selling compute to Anthropic at ~$14.5B/GW/year), and how regulatory headwinds from midterm elections may constrain future data center expansion. The valuation framework — behind a partial paywall — ties these cost dynamics into a full returns-on-capital and DCF-style model.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors, this granular GW-level cost build provides a rare bottoms-up framework for stress-testing whether Meta's unprecedented AI capex translates into defensible earnings power — directly actionable for anyone sizing or modeling META exposure.

articles.headline: Building pharma's laboratory of the future
articles.summary: McKinsey examines how pharmaceutical companies are rebuilding laboratory operations around AI, automation, and advanced data infrastructure to accelerate R&D productivity. The piece treats the 'lab of the future' as an operational imperative rather than a speculative vision, covering drug discovery workflows, experimental data management, and the organizational changes required to capture AI-driven efficiency gains. It offers a strategic framework for how pharma R&D infrastructure is being restructured end-to-end.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors in CRO, CDMO, and biopharma names, this provides a consulting-grade map of where capital and competitive differentiation are flowing in pharma R&D — directly informing thesis work on which platform players and infrastructure enablers stand to benefit.
